slides.title: VSX3000 Performance Testing: Test Procedure and Robot Program
slides.subtitle: Running the five capture series and what the robot program must do
slides.notes: This deck walks through the technician procedure for the VSX3000 characterization session: preparation, registration, the plan, the five capture series, the pose log and manifest, the checks, and the deliverables. It follows sections 3 to 15 of the procedure; the targets and fixtures are in the procurement and build deck and in section 1. The analysis definitions are in the characterization specification; the procedure says how to capture, not how to compute.

slides.title: What we are measuring, and why

columns.head: The five series
points: A: depth noise against distance, incidence angle and drift, on the board
B: lateral resolution from the edge targets, at two step heights
Z: the smallest detectable depth step and the depth quantum
C: true against sensed area of disks and cutouts
D: the minimum detectable feature size, as a detection probability

columns.head: What the robot gives us
points: Commanded, repeatable, logged target poses in front of a fixed sensor
Ground truth in the sensor frame through one registration from the board's plane
Read-back poses at 0.01 mm: the step truth of series Z
Every pose approached from the same direction, so backlash enters no comparison

columns.head: What the session produces
points: One session folder of raw .mc frames with a manifest that says, for every file, which target was where
Six analyses that write forward_model_parameters.json, the hand-off to the forward-noise simulator
Analysis E, boundary bias, reuses the B and C frames and needs no captures of its own

slides.message: If the manifest is wrong, the results are wrong: much of the procedure is about getting that table right.
slides.notes: Figure 1 of the procedure gives the order and the dependencies: registration feeds every analysis, the noise level from A sets the thresholds of B, C and D, the edge spread function from B predicts the area bias measured in C, and E reuses the B and C frames. Series run in the order A, B, Z, C, D without moving the sensor between them.

slides.title: One session folder, 7,202 poses, 42,920 frames

stats.label: robot poses in the default plan, in the planner's order
of robot time at 10 frames per second and 3 s per move; two to three working days with swaps, checks and warm-up
of .mc frames at 10 GB per 1,000 frames; check storage before starting

slides.message: Save every frame raw, with one manifest row per frame, so any analysis can be re-run without re-capturing.
slides.body: The default plan is the capture budget of procedure section 13. Outside it are the optional captures the engineer plans only when needed: the filters-off repeat of A and B, the staircase of Z, the lateral sweep of B, the open-background variant of C, and the separate 8 hour drift run taken with the robot idle.
slides.notes: The budget assumes a frame rate of 10 frames per second and 3 seconds per move plus settle; the VSX3000 frame rate in the chosen trigger mode replaces them. The extended 5 percent detection series takes about a third of the robot time; the engineer can halve it by lowering the extended trials from 300 to 150, at the cost of a wider interval on the 5 percent point. Section 13 of the procedure has the budget table per series.

slides.title: The session at a glance

steps.head: Prepare
steps.text: Loggers on; sensor configuration fixed and recorded; warm-up until the plane Z stops drifting; settle check

steps.head: Register
steps.text: 30 hand-jogged poses of the board; the plane-correspondence solve; accept at 0.15 mm RMS or better

steps.head: Plan
steps.text: plan_stations writes poses.csv, the summary and the picture; record the seed

steps.head: Series A and B
steps.text: Noise on the board, then edges on T3a and T3b at both gaps

steps.head: Series Z
steps.text: Step ladder and ramp on the board, every pose approached from below

steps.head: Series C and D
steps.text: Areas and detection trials on T4 and T5 at both gaps

steps.head: Hand over
steps.text: Pose log, manifest, checks, session log, environment log, photos

slides.notes: Every target swap is followed by the mount check of step 4.8, and the planner has already placed drift sentinels in the pose list before series A, every 60 minutes, and after the last pose of each series, on whatever target is mounted at that moment. Tell the engineer at once if a series stops early; later series depend on earlier ones.

slides.title: Preparation before the first session

columns.head: Robot
points: Flange confirmed against ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6; repeatability 0.05 mm or better
Controller reports the actual pose at 0.01 mm with a time stamp
Each fixture weighed; tool load data entered
Robot program written to the pose-list interface; dry run of every pose at reduced speed with the largest target
Safety review

columns.head: Sensor and computers
points: Capture software set for the trigger and the pose-id file names
Production sensor configuration chosen and recorded in sensor_config.json; filters-off repeat decided
At least 430 GB free on the capture computer
This repository installed on the analysis computer and self-tested

columns.head: Cell
points: Layout study: target centers from 400 to 1600 mm, the five field positions and tilts to 45 degrees inside the robot's reach, before the sensor mount is fixed
Run-out base plate bolted to the table
Robot base frame identified and recorded; temperature loggers started and their clocks checked

slides.message: The targets, the adapter and the tools themselves are in the procurement and build deck and in section 1 of the procedure.
slides.notes: Section 1f of the procedure. Once the robot model and controller are settled, the robot program can be written with Claude Code to the interface of section 11. The dry run must include the 2 mm back-off below each series Z pose and the approach retreat of every other pose.

slides.title: The sensor stays fixed; the robot carries the target
points: The sensor stands on its own rigid mount, mechanically separate from the robot base; a bump means a new session
The robot carries the target on the adapter anywhere between 400 and 1600 mm, the working range of the test
The laboratory is enclosed and its lighting constant: no light meter, no ambient-light log, no changes during the session
Sensor-housing and air temperatures are logged every minute into environment_log.csv
The origin of every pose is the optical center of the left IR camera; H and V are the image axes, Z the optical axis
slides.notes: Figure 2 of the procedure. The robot must report its actual, encoder-derived flange pose at the capture time, to 0.01 mm, time-stamped against the frames; if it cannot, tell the engineer before starting, because for series Z the read-back pose is the step truth. Do not change the active base frame, the exposure or any sensor setting during the session.

slides.title: Configuration, warm-up, settle and frame checks

cards.head: Sensor configuration (engineer)
cards.text: Auto-exposure off; exposure, gain, emitter power and trigger mode fixed; every filter setting, the SDK and firmware versions in sensor_config.json under a config_id

cards.head: Warm-up
cards.text: Power for at least 45 minutes; then the board at 800 mm, 10 frames every minute, until the mean plane Z drifts less than 0.1 of its temporal noise over 10 minutes

cards.head: Settle and vibration
cards.text: At 400 mm, 100 frames with the servos on after a move and 100 with the brakes on; raise the 2 s settle time or stiffen the mount if the servo-on noise exceeds the brakes-on noise by more than 10 percent

cards.head: Intrinsics and frame checks (engineer)
cards.text: Dagger values from the SDK into sensor_config.json; valid depth at 400 and 1600 mm; depth registered to the left IR image within 0.5 px; baseline direction from the occlusion band

slides.caption: Procedure section 3. Whatever settle time passes the check is the one the robot program uses; write the date, serial numbers, versions, base frame and plate reports in session_log.md.
slides.notes: The optional separate drift run also belongs here: on the same day or the day before, the board on a fixed stand at 800 mm, the sensor powered from cold, 30 frames every 2 minutes for 8 hours with the loggers running and nothing touched. It measures the sensor's own drift against its temperature; the sentinels in the session stay required because only they see the robot and the mounts.

slides.title: Registration: 30 hand-jogged poses of the board

steps.head: Mount
steps.text: The board on its adapter; mount check

steps.head: Jog
steps.text: To each of the 30 registration poses of the plan: 400 to 1600 mm, across the field, tilted about H and V up to plus or minus 20 degrees, the board fully visible

steps.head: Capture
steps.text: 10 depth frames and the read-back robot pose at each; files named by the rule of section 5

steps.head: Solve (engineer)
steps.text: Fit the plane of each capture; register --observations observations.csv --out registration.json

stats.label: expected standard error of the camera's Z offset, recorded with the result

slides.message: If the residual is larger, add poses with larger tilts or check the mount, then solve again. Registration comes first, so the poses are jogged by hand; the exact pose is solved afterward.
slides.notes: Procedure section 4. The plane-correspondence solve fixes the camera's pose in the robot base from the depth planes alone: no pattern plate, no IR image, no emitter switching. What planes cannot observe, the sideways position of a target on the flange, comes from the as-built datum and the once-per-mount check against the left IR image. The registration's translation cancels in series Z, which is a difference of registered poses.

slides.title: The mount check after every target swap
points: Move the mounted target to the mount-check station, 800 mm, centered and fronto-parallel; capture a few frames into a folder of their own
check_captures --mount-check fits the front plane and compares it with the registered pose: Z within 0.15 mm, tilt within 0.05 degrees
For a feature target it also locates one feature outline in the image and compares H and V with the as-built datum offsets: within 0.5 px
PASS or FAIL per check with the measured value; otherwise re-seat the target or correct the datum record
The spigot and dowel return every target to the same datum, so a passed check makes re-mounting safe
slides.notes: Procedure step 4.8. The check frames are not part of the plan and need no pose-log lines; keep them in mount_check_<target>/ in the session folder. The tool reads targets.json, targets_asbuilt.csv and parameters.json from the folder of registration.json. For the board, which has no features, H and V are skipped and the verdict says so.

slides.title: One plan, 9 stations, 5 field positions

stats.label: stations of one geometric ladder, 400 to 1600 mm at a ratio of 2 to the quarter power
field positions: the center and four corners at 0.6 of the half field
logged in session_log.md; the same seed and inputs give the same plan again

slides.caption: The default plan: target centers in the sensor frame, side and front views, colored by series. Each cloud around a station is a set of random lateral offsets.
slides.notes: Procedure section 5. Run plan_stations once the registration is accepted and the sensor values are in sensor_config.json; it writes poses.csv, plan_summary.txt, plan.png, targets.json and parameters.json. Read plan_summary.txt before starting: it lists every pose the coverage rule pulled inward, every adjustment and every warning. Decide the optional captures before the first capture and plan once; adding the filters-off repeat, the open-background variant or the C-frame reuse later changes the random offsets of later series.

slides.title: Which series visits which stations
points: All 9 stations: series A, C and D, and the ramp of Z; A adds the legacy depths 700 and 1000 mm at the center
Every second station, the 5 shape stations 400, 566, 800, 1131 and 1600 mm: series B
Every fourth station, the 3 reduced stations 400, 800 and 1600 mm: the step ladder of Z; the tilt sub-series of A at 476, 800 and 1600 mm
The 3 farthest stations: the extended detection trials of D
The reference station 800 mm: warm-up check, sentinels, mount check, field sub-series of C, open-background variant, lateral sweep
slides.notes: Figure 6 of the procedure. A target that would not fit the field at a corner is pulled inward by the coverage rule and the achieved field fraction is logged in the row; do not move it back out. The tilt sub-series cannot run at 400 mm with the 200 x 150 mm board because the tilted board's near edge would come closer than the near limit, so the planner moves that sweep to 476 mm.

slides.title: What the robot program must do

columns.head: Inputs
points: poses.csv from the planner: one row per pose in execution order, with the wanted target pose in the camera frame and the flange pose from the registration
The settle time of step 4.4, 2 s unless the check raised it

columns.head: Behavior
points: Joint move to a point short of the pose along the approach, then a linear move onto it: from below in Z and from the negative side of H and V, every pose, every series
Series Z: back off 2 mm toward smaller Z, then move up onto the pose
Never change the base frame, the speed settings or the sensor configuration

columns.head: Outputs
points: Trigger the row's frames through the capture software, named from the row by the rule of section 5 (procedure, target, gap, station, field, pose, frame; the example is on the next slide)
Append the REPORTED flange pose, the temperatures and a time stamp to the pose log; note where it is written

slides.message: Once the robot model and controller are settled, the robot program can be written with Claude Code.
slides.notes: Procedure section 5, robot program outline, and section 11 for the pose log. The one exception to the approach rule is the optional lateral sweep of series B, where odd-numbered poses approach from the negative side and even-numbered from the positive side, so that hysteresis can be measured; the row says so in its approach_direction note.

slides.title: The per-pose loop

steps.head: Move
steps.text: Joint move to the approach point, linear move onto the pose, always from the same side

steps.head: Settle
steps.text: Wait the settle time for vibration to die out

steps.head: Capture
steps.text: The row's frames, named from the row: for example C_T5_G15_Z0800_F0_P017_f03.mc

steps.head: Log
steps.text: Read the actual, encoder-derived flange pose and append it with the temperatures and a time stamp

stats.label: assumed per move plus settle in the budget
assumed frame rate; the real one replaces it

slides.message: Follow the order column. Do not choose stations, positions or order yourself, and do not delete any frames.
slides.notes: Procedure section 5. Pose numbers have three digits; the optional captures planned outside the budget number their poses from 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000 and 5000 and so have four. A target without a back plate (the board) writes G0 in the file name.

slides.title: Series A and B: the board, then the edge targets

cards.head: A, noise on the board
cards.text: All 9 stations at the 5 field positions plus the legacy depths at the center, in randomized order; then the tilt sub-series at 476, 800 and 1600 mm (0, 15, 30, 45 degrees about V then H, 50 frames); then dismount, re-mount and repeat the 800 mm center station

cards.head: B, edges
cards.flag: T3a then T3b, 30 frames per pose
cards.text: At each of the 5 shape stations: 1 nominal pose and 25 jitter poses with logged random offsets up to plus or minus 4 px; the gap at 15 mm, then at 60 mm; the square's 5 degree slant is part of the target

cards.head: Sentinels
cards.text: Captured on whatever target is mounted, before A, every 60 minutes, after the last pose of each series; never swap a target for one

cards.head: Optional
cards.text: The filters-off repeat of A and B with a new config_id; the lateral sweep of T3a at 800 mm, 20 poses in H and 20 in V in 0.1 px steps, approached from alternating sides

slides.caption: Procedure sections 6 and 7. Each target stays mounted as long as the plan allows; the mount check follows every swap.
slides.notes: The random lateral offsets sample every sub-pixel phase of each edge; the plan holds them in millimeters so the robot only executes the row. Comparing the two gaps tests whether the normalized edge response depends on step height. The left and right edges of the square have opposite occlusion geometry relative to the baseline, which is why both polarities and all four edges are captured.

slides.title: Series Z: step ladder and ramp, approached from below

steps.text: Mount the board centered and fronto-parallel; mount check; every pose of the series backs off 2 mm and moves up onto its pose
Step ladder at 400, 800 and 1600 mm: six rungs of 0.25 to 8 expected quanta, never below 0.1 mm; alternate Z0 and Z0 plus the step for 10 cycles, 10 frames per visit
Ramp at all 9 stations: the board tilted about H so the true depth across its height spans 3 expected quanta, 0.4 degrees near to 7.1 degrees far; 50 frames; the tilt is in the row
Log the read-back pose as it is: it is the step truth; never correct it by hand
Optional staircase, planned later with the same seed, only if the ramp measured a quantum of at least 0.1 mm

slides.notes: Procedure section 8 and Figure 8. The true step between two visits is the difference of their registered front-plane depths, so the registration's translation cancels and only the robot's relative motion matters; the smallest rung, 0.1 mm, is twice the robot repeatability. The ramp finds the quantum without small Z moves: each image row lies at one true depth and the rows step through the quanta.

slides.title: Series C and D: areas and detection trials

columns.head: C, areas
points: T4 and T5, each gap, all 9 stations, centered: 30 poses of 10 frames with random offsets
Field sub-series at 800 mm and the small gap: the four corners, 10 poses each, pulled inward where needed
Optional open-background variant at 800 mm: back plate off, 800 mm of clear space behind the holes

columns.head: D, detection trials
points: One frame per pose at a fresh random offset: one trial for every feature and blank site on the plate at once
60 trials per feature and station; 300 at the 3 farthest stations for the 5 percent level
Shuffled order with a logged seed; the first frame of each C pose may count as a trial if the engineer asked for it

columns.head: Rules
points: Never use two frames of one pose as two trials
Post check first: check_captures --pilot 800 on the first C frames; posts seen above the false-alarm rate are remade thinner
Keep frame f00 of every C pose

slides.message: The detection levels are the feature-and-station pairs: 27 values of subtended size, spaced by the station ratio, overlapping by half an octave.
slides.notes: Procedure sections 9 and 10. Sensed area depends on where a feature's edge falls relative to the pixel grid and the projector dots, so the random offsets average over the phase and also measure its spread. The 0 percent detection level is not measured; the analysis predicts it from the fitted curve below the 5 percent point and labels it a prediction. If time is short, 150 extended trials still measure the 5 percent level, to about plus or minus 3.5 percent.

slides.title: The pose log and the manifest

columns.head: What the log holds, per pose
points: procedure, target_id, gap_mm, station_z_mm, field, pose_index, frames: exactly the plan row, which also names the files
x_mm, y_mm, z_mm: the REPORTED flange position in the base frame, at least 2 decimals
rotation_type and r1 to r9: the orientation in the controller's own form
timestamp, sensor_temp_c, air_temp_c

columns.head: Rotation forms the tools accept
points: quaternion_wxyz (ABB) or quaternion_xyzw
euler_zyx_deg: KUKA A, B, C
fixed_xyz_deg: FANUC W, P, R
rotvec_deg: Universal Robots, in degrees
matrix: nine numbers, row by row
make_manifest converts them all and names every file or pose that does not match

slides.notes: Procedure section 11. After the session the engineer runs make_manifest with the pose log, the capture folder, the plan and the registration; it matches every file to its plan row by name, takes the read-back pose from the log and computes the target pose in the camera frame. A pose without files or a file without a pose is a warning; problems in the log or plan stop the tool. Never use poses.csv as the pose log: it holds the commanded poses, and the analysis needs the reported ones. A log rounded to 0.1 mm makes the smallest Z rungs meaningless.

slides.title: Check each series while the targets are still set up

cards.head: Low valid fraction
cards.flag: below half of the target's pixels
cards.text: Exposure, or the target was outside the field

cards.head: Outline crossing the border
cards.flag: a disk, cutout or square cut off
cards.text: The pose is unusable; ask the engineer to re-plan it slightly inward

cards.head: Target not in the field
cards.text: The manifest or the registration is wrong for that pose

cards.head: Plane fit or plane position
cards.flag: residual too large; plane far from the registered one
cards.text: A wrongly classified plane, a wrong pose, a wrong registration or a target that moved; the limits are loose on purpose

cards.head: Normal disagrees
cards.text: A tilted mount or a wrong pose

slides.caption: check_captures --session <folder> --out check.json prints one line per pose and a verdict; exit code 0 means nothing flagged. Re-capture flagged poses under a new pose_index; never delete lines from the log.
slides.notes: Procedure section 12. Run the quick check as soon as a series is complete, while the robot and targets are still set up, so that a flagged pose can be re-captured without a re-mount. The same tool does the mount check (--mount-check) and the post check of series D (--pilot 800). Its limits are options listed in appendix B.

slides.title: Things that spoil a session

items.text: Moving or bumping the sensor: everything after it is a new session
Changing exposure, gain, any filter, the base frame or the lighting mid-session
Logging the commanded pose instead of the reported one, or rounding it to 0.1 mm: for series Z the read-back pose is the step truth
Approaching a series Z pose from above or from different directions: backlash then enters the difference between visits
A loose adapter, a loosened standoff or a target shifted on its spigot: do the mount check after every swap; never swap a target to take a sentinel
Fingerprints, dust or gloss on a target, or different finishes on front and back plates: wipe with isopropyl alcohol
Using two frames of one pose as two detection trials; skipping the warm-up or shortening the settle wait; losing the plan's seed

slides.notes: Procedure section 15, which also tabulates the sources of error: robot repeatability and absolute accuracy, the registration residual, the plane-registration depth offset, the as-built uncertainties, plate flatness, thermal drift, interreflection, the sensor's temporal filter. The relative measurements are robust; the smallest Z steps and the absolute bias are the ones most limited by the setup.

slides.title: What to hand over at the end of the session
checklist: Characterization_<YYYYMMDD>/ with every .mc file in its series sub-folder, named by the rule of section 5
sensor_config.json with every filter setting and the dagger values filled in; registration.json, accepted, with its residual in session_log.md
targets_asbuilt.csv with the uncertainties; poses.csv, plan_summary.txt, plan.png, targets.json and parameters.json of the plan used, and the seed
The pose log, and manifest.csv produced by make_manifest without errors; check.json with no flags, or a note on each
environment_log.csv and the temperature logs; the drift run's 241 captures in sentinels/ if it was made
session_log.md: date, serial number, warm-up and settle times, base frame, plate flatness and finish, mount-check results, target changes with times, anything unusual
Photos of the sensor stand and of each target on the adapter (a phone camera is fine)

software.head: Software
points: plan_stations, make_manifest, check_captures, register and analyze in sensorperf.cli
Install and self-test: procedure appendix C; every tool prints its options with --help, quoted in appendix B
The engineer runs analyze on the finished folder; results go into analysis/

slides.notes: Procedure section 13. The engineer runs the six analyses in the order A, B, Z, C, D, E with one command; A supplies the noise level that B, C and D use, and B supplies the edge spread function that C compares with. The output forward_model_parameters.json is the hand-off to the forward-noise simulator.
